body:
`cuda.grid(1)` returns an incorrect value in the following code:

```py
import numpy as np
from numba import cuda


@cuda.jit
def bug(out):
    i = cuda.threadIdx.x + cuda.blockIdx.x * cuda.blockDim.x
    i2 = cuda.grid(1)
    if i != i2:
        # this shouldn't happen
        print(i, i2)


free_mem, _ = cuda.current_context().get_memory_info()
# max_num_parallel_iter is around 566281830 on my 4090
max_num_parallel_iter = free_mem // 4 - 128 * 1024 * 1024
dev_out = cuda.device_array(max_num_parallel_iter, dtype=np.float32)
bug[22121216, 256](dev_out)
```

One example of a case which is printed is when `i = 2147551327` and `i2 = -214741596`, which likely indicates a signed 32 bit integer overflow. The bug doesn't appear when setting `max_num_parallel_iter` to an integer constant, which must mean it's somehow related to the calculation from the memory info.
title: cuda.grid(1) returns incorrect value due to signed integer overflow
